editorial.headline: Footwear and Leather Repair: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Although nationally open to 100 per cent foreign ownership, this repair activity cannot be registered under PMA in Bali today.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity under PMA in Bali today, even though the national record opens it to 100 per cent foreign ownership. The activity covers repair and maintenance services for footwear and leather goods. The stated examples make the scope concrete: shoes, boots and sandals on the footwear side, and suitcases and bags among leather goods. Fitting shoe heels is expressly included, while shoe-shining is expressly outside the group. Both inclusions are part of the stated scope. The category is therefore defined by repair and maintenance of the identified goods, with its boundary stated directly rather than left to implication.

The national entry supplies both the scale and foreign-ownership position. It is open to PMA, and its stated foreign-ownership ceiling is 100 per cent. At the national level, a foreign stake may reach that 100 per cent ceiling. The activity is available at every scale named in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. The national PMA basis given for this position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The record therefore presents national availability across all of its listed scales, with the ceiling stated for the activity.

Bali must be read separately, because the local result is not a revised percentage but a block. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk position is recorded as Low/Medium-Low across every scope. Bali’s stated rule is an island-wide, permanent PMA moratorium for Low and Medium-Low risk classifications. The entry is accordingly marked BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO. Its stated reason is that the moratorium, recorded in May 2026, blocks the activity. That status carries the key local fact: PMA registration is blocked in Bali.

That produces a clear national-versus-Bali reading. Nationally, this is a PMA-open activity, with a foreign stake that may reach the recorded 100 per cent ceiling and availability across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. In Bali, the same activity cannot be registered under PMA because of the recorded risk-based moratorium. The national opening does not override the local block, and no lower Bali ownership ceiling is supplied instead. National openness cannot be read as permission to register this activity under PMA in Bali; under the recorded Bali position, it remains unavailable there today.
